subjects.authored_statement: Private keys and installation tokens never enter the repository, Git remotes, persistent Git configuration, process arguments, generated reports, or PR content.
The tool does not approve or merge pull requests and does not bypass the main ruleset.
The tool does not require organization, administration, secrets, workflow, or checks permissions.
A private key readable by group or other users is rejected.
Managing App managers or distributing private keys.
Automatic approval, merge, release, or workflow modification.
Governing how changes are implemented locally.
A maintainer can invoke one documented command from a local checkout to push the current change and create a GitHub pull request under the App identity.
The command obtains a short-lived installation token from a locally held App private key and removes local token material when it exits.
The command can request one or more human reviewers while leaving approval to GitHub's protected-branch rules.
App, installation, repository, branch, base, title, body, and reviewer inputs are explicit or supplied by documented non-secret defaults.
Failures identify the failed stage without printing private keys, JWTs, installation tokens, or credential-bearing URLs.
